B06_00: During gastrulation, primitive streak epiblast cells undergo epithelial-mesenchymal transition to form mesoderm, while a partial version yields definitive endoderm. FGF, WNT, NODAL and BMP signals converge on EOMES and TBXT, which induce SNAI1 to repress E-cadherin, occludin and claudins, so cells detach, ingress and adopt an N-cadherin mesenchymal programme. The same switch is reused in carcinoma, where TGF-beta-driven E-cadherin loss underlies invasion and metastasis.
B06_01: After fertilization, inherited chromatin states are erased to allow zygotic genome activation. The paternal genome is demethylated actively through TET3 oxidation, deamination and base excision repair, while in the maternal genome DPPA3 blocks TET3 and displaces UHRF1, so DNMT1 maintenance fails and methylation is lost passively. KDM5 and KDM6 demethylases remove H3K4me3 and H3K27me3; failure impairs preimplantation development and imprint handling.
B06_02: Lateral plate mesoderm arises from the primitive streak and builds heart, limbs, blood and body cavity and gut linings. Endodermal SHH and IHH induce FOXF1, which drives BMP4, and BMP4 with FOXF1 activates GATA4, forming a self-maintaining loop that locks in lateral identity. Disturbance of this loop underlies congenital heart and diaphragm defects, and the same signals derive cardiac and vascular lineages from stem cells.
B06_03: Cells ingressing at the anterior primitive streak form axial mesoderm, which becomes prechordal plate and notochord, stiffens the body axis, patterns neural tube and somites via Sonic Hedgehog, and later forms the nucleus pulposus involved in disc disease. NODAL-SMAD2/3 with FOXH1, TEAD-YAP1 and TBXT activates FOXA2, which drives NOTO and SHH. WNT input via CTNNB1, LEF1 and TCF7 positions this programme along the axis.
B06_04: The melanocyte transcription factor MITF-M also sets oxidative metabolism by inducing PPARGC1A, which drives mitochondrial biogenesis and favours oxidative phosphorylation over glycolysis. This axis helps explain melanoma survival under BRAF inhibition, whereas low-MITF, low-PPARGC1A tumours are more invasive and drug-tolerant. MITF also induces the NAD+-dependent deacetylase SIRT1, which supports proliferation and opposes senescence, linking lineage identity to energetics and phenotype switching.
B06_05: MITF-M drives a melanocyte survival programme through anti-apoptotic targets BCL2, BCL2A1 and BIRC7, allowing melanoblasts to migrate and colonise skin and melanocytes to persist; loss causes depigmentation, while persistence supports melanoma survival and therapy resistance. MITF also induces DICER1, and its target-derived miR-211 acts with Argonaute and TNRC6 silencing complexes. POU3F2 and SIN3A-HDAC1 corepressors restrain this output.
B06_06: MITF-M also directly represses genes for extracellular matrix, focal adhesion and EMT, determining whether melanoma cells proliferate or switch to an invasive, drug-resistant state. Lowering MITF-M releases targets such as ITGA2, paxillin, EDIL3, peroxidasin and SERPINE1, and regulators including ZEB1, SOX2, CDH1 and CDH2, driving cytoskeletal remodelling and migratory character. High MITF-M thus marks proliferative melanoma and low MITF-M invasive, therapy-resistant cells.
B06_07: During pregnancy, hormone receptor-negative luminal progenitors of the mammary gland give rise to milk-secreting alveolar cells, the alternative to ductal fate, enabling lactation. Notch, WNT and hormone signalling set this choice, with reduced Notch favouring alveolar identity and prolactin-STAT signalling driving differentiation and milk protein production, aided by myoepithelial modulation of Notch ligands. After weaning, surviving alveolar precursors reconstitute tissue later, linking to breast cancer origins.
B06_08: Basal mammary progenitors give rise to myoepithelial cells, contractile cells around ducts and alveoli that expel milk in response to oxytocin, deposit basement membrane and restrain luminal outgrowth. Strong EGF receptor stimulation by amphiregulin, EGF and TGF-alpha drives specification during ductal morphogenesis and organoid differentiation. Normally unipotent, these progenitors can regenerate luminal cells after luminal loss, licensed by EGFR together with Notch and Wnt signalling.
B06_09: Specification of the anterior neural plate begins brain formation, giving rise to forebrain and midbrain, and neural tube closure failure causes spina bifida. BMP inhibition by anterior visceral endoderm allows OTX2, ZIC2, POU3F1 and POU5F1 to activate SOX2 via an upstream enhancer, accompanied by SOX1, PAX6, ZEB2 and ZNF521 as pluripotency factors resolve. Reciprocal OTX2-GBX2 repression sets the midbrain-hindbrain boundary.
B06_10: Clearing maternal oocyte transcripts on schedule lets the embryo switch to its own gene products, and M-decay uses maternally stored factors; failure causes oocyte arrest, early cleavage stalling and infertility. ZFP36L2 in maturing oocytes and BTG4 after fertilization recruit the CCR4-NOT deadenylase to shorten poly(A) tails, with BTG4 linking to PABP and eIF4 cap-binding machinery. DICER1-derived siRNAs also guide AGO2 slicing of maternal mRNAs.
B06_11: Zygotic genome activation switches the transcriptionally silent embryo to its own transcription, following epigenetic remodelling, in minor one-cell and major eight-cell waves in humans; without it development arrests. DUX4, promoted by DPPA2 and DPPA4, activates early embryonic genes such as ZSCAN4, LEUTX, DUXA and KDM4E with CREBBP and EP300, and drives retroviral LTR and satellite repeat transcription. TUT4 and TUT7 clear maternal transcripts.
B06_12: MITF-M also maintains genome stability in proliferating melanocytes and melanoma cells by inducing MCM2 and MCM5 helicase subunits, the ligase LIG1, BRCA1 and the telomerase subunit TERT. MITF knockdown causes DNA damage accumulation and senescence, whereas ATF4-driven MITF suppression produces reversible arrest without senescence. The pathway links lineage identity to replication licensing and proliferative lifespan, central to melanoma switching between proliferative and invasive states.
B06_13: The mammary luminal lineage, comprising inner ductal cells and milk-secreting alveolar cells, arises from unipotent progenitors expanding during puberty and pregnancy and is the presumed origin of major breast cancer subtypes. Notch and steroid hormone signalling govern ductal versus alveolar fate, and progenitors retain plasticity. The EGF receptor ligands amphiregulin, EGF and TGF-alpha link systemic oestrogen to local proliferation, driving ductal elongation and branching with FGF cues.
B06_14: During pancreatic branching morphogenesis, undifferentiated duct-tree precursors must keep proliferating until some become endocrine cells, and disruption limits beta cell number, causing neonatal diabetes and hypoplasia. ONECUT1 sustains ONECUT3 and HNF1B to maintain progenitors, while NEUROG3 marks endocrine commitment. Notch signalling through NOTCH1, RBPJ, Mastermind-like coactivators and acetyltransferases induces HES1 to repress NEUROG3, rationing differentiation by lateral inhibition.
B06_15: MITF-M commits neural crest precursors to melanocyte fate, controlling pigmentation, melanoblast migration and survival, and melanoma behaviour. FOXD3, SOX2 and SNAI2 initially silence its promoter, while PAX3 and SOX10, reinforced by WNT/beta-catenin, endothelin, KIT ligand and MC1R-cAMP-CREB signalling, activate it; MITF-M then represses FOXD3 and SOX2. Phosphorylation, SUMOylation, ubiquitination, 14-3-3 binding, nuclear export and acetylation tune its activity.
B06_16: Epiblast cells ingressing through the anterior primitive streak become definitive endoderm, the source of gut tube, liver, pancreas, thyroid and lung epithelium. High NODAL-SMAD2/3/4 signalling induces EOMES, MIXL1 and goosecoid, and EOMES activates FOXA2, SOX17, GATA4 and GATA6. Unlike mesoderm, endoderm retains E-cadherin, with CDH1 and CXCR4 used to isolate it, and WNT input patterns the streak; this step underlies stem cell-derived hepatocytes and beta cells.
B06_17: Somitogenesis segments paraxial mesoderm into somites that form vertebrae, ribs, muscle and dermis, and its failure causes vertebral malformations such as spondylocostal dysostosis. A Notch-based oscillator, with HES7 autorepression and LFNG feedback shaped by DLL1 and DLL3, meets WNT, FGF and retinoic acid gradients at a determination front. There TBX6 and MSGN1 drive MESP2, which induces EPHA4 and RIPPLY2, while proteasomal turnover sustains oscillation.
B06_18: This transcriptional programme specifies and maintains early pancreatic bud precursors that become acini, ducts and islets; in mice loss causes agenesis or hypoplasia, and human mutations cause pancreatic and beta-cell developmental disorders including diabetes. HNF1B, ONECUT1 and PDX1, with mesenchymal FGF10, drive a second tier including PTF1A, ONECUT3, NR5A2 and NKX6-1. These begin separating acinar and endocrine fates, linking endodermal patterning to later cell identity.
B06_19: Gastrulation converts the epiblast into three germ layers via the primitive streak, laying out the body plan. NODAL-SMAD2/3/4 with TRIM33, BMP4 and WNT/beta-catenin position the streak and induce TBXT and EOMES, which with FOXH1, MIXL1 and GSC specify mesoderm and definitive endoderm while shutting down POU5F1, SOX2 and NANOG. Mesoderm forms by EMT and endoderm by a partial version; streak failure arrests the embryo.
B06_20: The neural plate border, between future brain and skin, gives rise to neural crest and cranial placodes, forming peripheral nerves, craniofacial skeleton, melanocytes, adrenal medulla, lens, inner ear and olfactory epithelium. Intermediate BMP and FGF with graded WNT, via BMP4, FGF4, WNT3A, beta-catenin and TCF7L1, position it. GBX2, TFAP2A paralogues, PAX3, PAX7, MSX1, DLX5 and ZIC1 cross-regulate into border identity; failure underlies neurocristopathies.
B06_21: Definitive endoderm is patterned into dorsal and ventral foregut buds that become multipotent pancreatic progenitors, later forming acinar, ductal and islet cells including beta cells. Dorsal and ventral endoderm pass through duodeno-pancreatic or hepato-pancreatic intermediates, with mesenchymal and notochord signals favouring pancreatic over hepatic fate. FGF10, FGF2, FGF4, FGF7 and EGF sustain progenitor expansion; failure causes pancreatic agenesis and neonatal diabetes, and these cues guide stem cell beta-cell production.
B06_22: Zygotic decay clears maternal transcripts using factors induced by the zygotic genome, allowing the embryo to take control of gene expression; failure stalls development and causes infertility. Partially deadenylated maternal mRNAs in closed-loop complexes are uridylated at their 3' ends by zygotically induced TUT4 and TUT7. The uridine tail recruits PABPN1, which brings in the exoribonuclease DIS3L2 to degrade the transcript, linking deadenylation, uridylation and decay.
B06_23: Bipotent pancreatic trunk progenitors enter a committed endocrine progenitor state able to make all islet cell types, a ductal versus endocrine choice set largely by mechanical environment. Fibronectin and vitronectin acting through integrin alpha5beta1 promote spreading and a YAP1-NOTCH axis that represses endocrine commitment, while collagens and laminins favour confinement, allowing NEUROG3 to rise and SOX9 and ONECUT1 to fall. EGF also restrains NEUROG3, informing stem cell diabetes therapies.
B06_24: The interfollicular epidermis is continually renewed by keratinocytes moving upward through layers, forming the cornified barrier against pathogens and water loss. Basal stem cells generate transit amplifying cells that progress through spinous and granular stages to corneocytes, which lose organelles and are shed. Microenvironmental cues, notably EGF signalling favouring basal proliferation, balance renewal against differentiation; disruption underlies barrier-defective skin disease, impaired wound repair and keratinocyte tumours.
B06_25: Insulin and growth factor signalling suppress a FOXO1-driven stress and starvation programme of gluconeogenesis, autophagy, cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. AKT isoforms activated downstream of PI3K phosphorylate FOXO1 at several sites, promoting 14-3-3 binding and nuclear exclusion. This branch lowers hepatic glucose output and permits growth, its dysregulation contributes to insulin resistance and hyperglycaemia, and constitutive AKT in tumours keeps tumour-suppressive FOXO1 inactive.
B06_26: MITF-M also sets melanocytic cell motility and invasiveness through targets such as CEACAM1, the formin DIAPH1 and GMPR, tuning adhesion and actin, and via SNAI2-linked EMT programmes. In melanoma, cells switch between MITF-high proliferative and MITF-low invasive states, so MITF activity influences local growth versus metastasis and targeted therapy response. The same control underlies normal melanoblast migration, linking lineage identity to motility.
B06_27: MITF-M acts as a rheostat on the cell cycle: intermediate activity drives proliferation via CDK2, cyclin D1, cyclin B1, CDC25B, PLK1 and MET; low activity causes dedifferentiation, slower cycling and invasion; and high activity induces p21 and p16 arrest. This underlies melanocyte biology and melanoma phenotype switching independent of pigmentation. Wnt-responsive TCF/LEF with beta-catenin feeds the same promoters, while TBX2 and SIN3A-HDAC1 provide repression.
B06_28: Mammary stem cells arise from embryonic surface ectoderm and found the ductal tree, regenerating functional glands and producing luminal and myoepithelial progeny; in adult human breast they are rare and concentrated in terminal ductal lobular units. They drive placode and bud formation, pubertal outgrowth and pregnancy remodelling, and when misregulated, stem-like breast cancer compartments. FGF10 signalling, with Wnt, Hedgehog, Notch and ovarian hormones, generates and maintains them.
B06_29: Sperm DNA is compacted with protamines, and after fertilization the male pronucleus must be rebuilt with oocyte-supplied histones to decondense, become transcriptionally permissive and join early divisions. SRPK1 phosphorylates PRM1 and PRM2, promoting their removal by NPM2 and recruiting HIRA, which deposits H3.3 with H2B, H4, H2AX and the oocyte linker histone H1-8, aided by METTL23 methylation. Defects contribute to fertilization failure.
B06_30: Besides pigmentation, MITF-M drives lysosome biogenesis by inducing nearly all vacuolar H+-ATPase subunits, which acidify lysosomes and endosomes for hydrolase activity, cargo degradation, receptor recycling and melanosome maturation. This output supports autophagic flux and survival of nutrient-starved melanoma cells. MITF also induces the lysosomal acid ceramidase ASAH1, linking sphingolipid handling to melanoma proliferation and drug resistance.
B06_31: Monocytes arise in bone marrow, exit to blood via CCR2, and within days die or enter tissues to become macrophages and dendritic cells. Classical CD14-high monocytes kill bacteria, non-classical CD16-high monocytes patrol vessels and sense viruses, and an intermediate state presents antigen. M-CSF via CSF1R drives survival and differentiation while T and NK cell interferon gamma licenses activation; excess drives inflammatory influx in atherosclerosis, autoimmunity and chronic infection.
B06_32: Nephron formation during fetal life sets lifelong nephron number, starting where ureteric bud tips meet metanephric mesenchyme. Bud-derived WNT9B induces WNT4 and mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition into polarised renal vesicles, while progenitors self-renew; WT1 permits proximal podocyte fate, and LHX1 and POU3F3 specify distal segments. HNF1B activates Notch components and IRX1/2 during comma- and S-shaped body formation, and HNF4A supports proximal tubule; defects cause congenital kidney malformation.
B06_33: Neurogenin 3 commits pancreatic progenitors to endocrine islet fates instead of duct and acinar fates; without it no islet hormone cells form, and human mutations cause malabsorptive diarrhoea with permanent neonatal diabetes. As a short-lived pioneer factor, NEUROG3 induces PAX4, NEUROD1, NKX2-2 and INSM1, which consolidate endocrine identity, drive cell cycle exit and bias hormone subtypes, converting a brief pulse into stable differentiation.
B06_34: MITF-M drives the melanocyte pigmentation programme for skin, hair and eye colour; loss causes hypopigmentation and deafness syndromes, and reactivation sustains differentiated melanoma. MITF binds M-box promoters of tyrosinase, TYRP1, DCT, MLANA, PMEL and GPR143, and induces RAB27A, MYO5A and melanophilin for melanosome transport to keratinocytes. Partners SOX10, TFAP2A, LEF1 with beta-catenin, CREB1 and IRF4, plus BAF chromatin remodellers, link it to Wnt and stress signalling.
B06_35: Intermediate mesoderm gives rise to the urogenital system, so its specification determines whether kidneys and reproductive tracts form; defects cause renal agenesis. Graded BMP sets its medial-lateral position, while Wnt, FGF and retinoic acid set its axial position. OSR1 and LHX1 mark it first, followed by mutually reinforcing PAX2 and PAX8, while FOXC1 and FOXC2 in paraxial mesoderm confine it; these cues direct stem cells toward kidney lineages.
B06_36: The posterior neural plate forms the hindbrain and anterior spinal cord, and incomplete neural tube closure causes defects such as spina bifida. Its caudal part derives from neuromesodermal progenitors, where WNT3A and FGF8 drive SOX2 through a posterior enhancer while TBX6 diverts sister cells to paraxial mesoderm. GBX2-OTX2 mutual repression sets the midbrain-hindbrain boundary, with SOX1, ZEB2 and POU3F1 accompanying neural commitment.
B06_37: The nephric duct, source of kidney and much of the male reproductive tract, epithelialises from intermediate mesoderm to form the pronephric and Wolffian ducts, from which the ureteric bud emerges. Retinoic acid via HOXB4 positions it, PAX2, PAX8 and LHX1 mark progenitors, and an LHX1-GATA3 loop drives EMX2, ID4, nephronectin and RET. RET responds to GDNF and nephronectin engages integrin alpha8beta1; failure causes renal agenesis and urinary tract anomalies.
B06_38: Pancreatic ductal cells line the branching duct tree carrying acinar secretions and bicarbonate, arising from bipotent trunk progenitors and earlier multipotent progenitors, and mature cells bear apical cilia and microvilli. The genes here form the matrix: fibrillar collagens, fibronectin and vitronectin build stroma, while laminins and collagen IV form the basement membrane that polarises epithelium and positions duct versus endocrine choice. Disturbed duct identity underlies cystic disease and ductal adenocarcinoma.
B06_39: The permanent kidney begins when the ureteric bud grows from the nephric duct into metanephric mesenchyme to form ureter and collecting ducts and induce nephrons; budding errors cause renal agenesis, duplex or dysplastic kidneys. Nephronectin engages integrin alpha8/beta1 to induce GDNF, acting through RET and GFRA1 to induce WNT11. PAX2, EYA1, SIX1/2, SALL1 and HOX11 specify mesenchyme, while SLIT2-ROBO2, BMP4-gremlin and FOXC1/2 restrict budding to one site.
